correctness.rationale: Writing a monotone data vector through its nonnegative increments turns the quadrature value into a linear function over a simplex, so its exact extrema are the prefix/tail sums of the symmetric weight vector. Symmetry converts the minimum to \(m_n=\min(0,\min P_k)\) and the maximum to \(1-m_n\), proving the general iff criterion. Exact moment-system reconstruction independently reproduced all proper prefix minima through \(n=13\): every \(n\le11\) is nonnegative, \(P_6=-147227/750750\) at \(n=12\), and the \(n=13\) minimum is positive. The published coefficient table independently agrees with the \(n=12\) exact weights, and the verifier constructs a strictly increasing positive witness for the undershoot.

value.rationale: Whether a quadrature rule maps monotone bounded samples back into their physical data range is a natural stability property distinct from coefficient positivity. The theorem supplies an exact general criterion and locates a nonmonotone first-failure/recovery boundary, so it is more than a coefficient-table recomputation.

final_claim: For normalized closed Newton–Cotes rules applied to bounded nondecreasing samples, range preservation is equivalent to nonnegativity of all proper cumulative weights; the first failure is the 13-point rule with 12 panels, whose sharp undershoot is \(147227/750750\), while the 14-point rule with 13 panels restores range preservation.
